clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 3082-3391 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8529.txt; 5 FR 3403, issue of Friday, August 30, 1940): signed August 27, 1940 under the act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847). It revokes Executive Order No. 4901 of June 4, 1928, which withdrew public land for classification and in aid of legislation in New Mexico, and says it becomes effective on "the sixtieth day from the date hereof." Its one command is a revocation, performed when it took effect; it has no term and no continuing duty. First end: performance on the effective date. The date is computed, not stated: the sixtieth day after August 27, 1940, excluding the signing day, is October 26, 1940 (4 days to August 31, 30 to September 30, 26 to October 26). If the signing day were counted as day 1 the date would be October 25, 1940; I record October 26 and disclose the alternative. No earlier end: the order had no effect before its effective date and no held text suspends or revokes it.

savings.reason: From the effective date the withdrawal made by Executive Order No. 4901 no longer applied by force of that order. That consequence persists independently of this order once the command was performed. Whether the lands were open to entry afterwards depends on other withdrawals and statutes not examined here; this claim does not decide it.
